sources.title: Madawi Al-Rasheed, Society and politics, 1744 to 1818 and 1824 to 1891
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis defining the paired First and Second Saudi State scope, Ottoman context, Najdi society, and political chronology.

sources.title: A History of Saudi Arabia, chapter sample
sources.note: Cambridge sample on Diriyah farmers, merchants, artisans, scholars, enslaved people, dates, livestock, coastal dependence, and long-distance trade.

sources.title: A History of Saudi Arabia, second edition chronology
sources.note: Cambridge chronology for rulers, expansion, Diriyah destruction, Riyadh restoration, Ottoman occupation of al-Ahsa, and Rashidi victory.

sources.title: Al Saud rulers in Riyadh, 1824 to 1891
sources.note: Cambridge appendix securing the Second Saudi State period and succession in Riyadh.

sources.title: Arabians for guns: Wahhabi matchlocks, world trade, and the rise of the first Saudi state
sources.note: Peer-reviewed evidence on firearms, caravan imports, exports, mobilization, enslaved labor, siege damage, and limits of gunmaking legends.

sources.title: The Saudis as Managers of the Hajj
sources.note: Cambridge chapter on Najdi pilgrimage restrictions, First Saudi control of the holy cities, seven Hajj seasons, and contested reforms.

sources.title: Civil War, Foreign Intervention, and the Question of Political Legitimacy
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of the post-1865 Saudi civil war, foreign intervention, juristic choices, and the Second State demise.

sources.title: Arabia to the end of the First World War
sources.note: Cambridge regional synthesis emphasizing nineteenth-century Najd connections toward Iraq rather than isolation.

sources.title: The tribal partners of empire in Arabia: the Ottomans and the Rashidis of Najd, 1880 to 1918
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of Ottoman-Rashidi partnership, Rashidi regional power, Saudi decline, and Abd al-Rahman in exile.

sources.title: A History of Saudi Arabia, introduction
sources.note: Cambridge discussion of repeated Arabian state formation, conquest, political fragility, and the distinction between earlier Saudi polities and the 1932 kingdom.

sources.title: Kadizadeli Ottoman Scholarship, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and the Rise of the Saudi State
sources.note: Oxford study of scholarly travel, ijazas, competing Najdi scholarship, the 1744 alliance, and Kitab al-Tawhid.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia: A Country Study
sources.note: Library of Congress historical synthesis on the alliance, Diriyah, 1818 destruction, reform persistence, local politics, and later restoration.

sources.title: The Seven Independent Arabian States: Nejd
sources.note: Digitized India Office handbook describing Faisal, succession conflict, Ottoman al-Ahsa, Rashidi victories, and the 1891 ending.

sources.title: Precis of Nejd Affairs, 1804 to 1904
sources.note: Contemporary imperial compilation on the post-1865 civil war, Ottoman intervention, al-Ahsa, and rival claims.

sources.title: Notes relating to Lewis Pellys Visit to Riyadh
sources.note: Digitized 1865 travel and intelligence notes on Faisal ibn Turki, Riyadh, geography, antiquities, and evidentiary bias.

sources.title: Boundaries of South-Eastern Arabia and Qatar, historical precis
sources.note: India Office retrospective on First Saudi expansion, Egyptian conquest, Gulf policy, and territorial uncertainty.

sources.title: Historical note on the Wahhabi movement and Nejd
sources.note: Digitized India Office history of Ibrahim Pashas 1818 conquest, Diriyahs destruction, occupation, and later Saudi restoration.

sources.title: UNESCO, At-Turaif District in ad-Diriyah
sources.note: World Heritage evidence on the first Saudi capital, oasis edge, palaces, urban fabric, Najdi architecture, and religious role.

sources.title: At-Turaif District in ad-Diriyah, nomination text
sources.note: Detailed heritage evidence on mud brick, plaster, stone, timber, palm matting, courtyards, majlis rooms, roofs, wells, and toilet towers.

sources.title: At-Turaif criteria for nomination
sources.note: UNESCO description of high ventilation openings, toilet towers, courtyards, oasis wells, water table, clay, and social urban form.

sources.title: UNESCO decision 34 COM 8B.15 on At-Turaif
sources.note: World Heritage Committee decision on adobe adaptation, wells operated by animals, oasis settlement, and heritage significance.

sources.title: UNESCO, Al-Ahsa Oasis, an Evolving Cultural Landscape
sources.note: World Heritage evidence on date palms, canals, springs, wells, drainage, markets, crafts, and long-lived oasis agriculture.

sources.title: Al-Ahsa Oasis nomination history
sources.note: Detailed evidence on traditional gravity and mugharraf irrigation, shallow groundwater, drainage, and small-scale cultivation.

sources.title: Saudipedia, Women in the First Saudi State
sources.note: Official heritage synthesis on women in teaching, commerce, crafts, household production, poetry, charity, and asylum.

sources.title: Saudipedia, Social Life in the First Saudi State
sources.note: Official heritage synthesis on extended households, gendered work, farming, pastoral movement, food, majlis gatherings, poetry, news, and games.

sources.title: Saudipedia, Quality of Life in the First Saudi State
sources.note: Official heritage synthesis on student endowments, teaching rooms, accommodation, markets, baths, agriculture, and architecture.

sources.title: Saudipedia, Markets in the First Saudi State
sources.note: Official heritage synthesis on al-Mawsim market, separate trading times or sections, livestock, jewelry, weapons, textiles, and lessons.

sources.title: Saudipedia, What Distinguishes the Traditional Najdi House?
sources.note: Heritage description of courtyard houses, indirect entrances, majlis and family stairs, one or two storeys, and connected walls.

sources.title: Saudi Founding Day historical guide
sources.note: Darah-backed official guide on Diriyah households, food, clothing, womens commerce, education, poetry, and source traditions.

sources.title: Guido Steinberg, Ecology, Knowledge, and Trade in Central Arabia
sources.note: European University Institute paper on Najdi books, manuscripts, copying, legal learning, expensive materials, and trade networks.

sources.title: Health Education in Saudi Arabia: Historical overview
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review locating organized state health services after this card and documenting later traditional healers, Quranic recitation, herbs, cautery, and cupping with chronological limits.

proposedOverrides.name: First and Second Saudi States in Najd
